title: Returned-Payment Fee on Benefit Overpayment Accounts — Console Reference
content:
When a repayment toward one of the Benefit Overpayment Accounts is returned unpaid by the bank, a returned-payment fee is owed for that return and is booked once, as its own fee component, on the same overpayment.

## What the booking records

Booking the fee adds one fee entry, of the amount booked, to the overpayment's ledger. The entry is a returned-payment fee, kept as the overpayment's fee component and tied to the confirmation number of the repayment that came back unpaid. The overpayment's balance due rises by the same amount. Nothing else on the overpayment changes. Once booked, the overpayment's ledger carries a returned-payment fee for that returned repayment, and the fee appears in the balance due.

| Before booking | After booking |
|---|---|
| A return entry for the repayment, with no fee entry carrying its confirmation number | A fee entry carrying the returned repayment's confirmation number |
| Balance due | Balance due plus the fee booked |

## The console tool

The fee is booked with `book_returned_payment_fee_10cb479c`. It is an agent-side tool of the Department's representative: the representative unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `overpayment_id` | The reference number of the benefit overpayment the returned repayment was made toward, as shown on the overpayment record returned by the overpayment lookup | Reference number |
| `payment_reference` | The confirmation number of the returned repayment exactly as it appears on that repayment's return entry in the overpayment ledger lookup | Copied character for character, with no change to letters, digits or punctuation |
| `fee_amount` | The fee to charge | USD, 2 decimal places, always positive; an amount with more decimals is rounded to the nearest cent when booked |

### Return

On success the tool returns a receipt with these items: `fee_entry_id` (the reference number of the new fee entry, present only when the fee was booked), `overpayment_id`, `payment_reference` (the returned repayment the fee is for), `fee_amount` (the fee booked, USD to 2 decimal places), `booked_on` (the booking date, YYYY-MM-DD) and `balance_due` (the overpayment's balance due including the fee). A receipt carrying a fee entry reference number means the fee is booked.

If the overpayment reference number matches no overpayment, the reply starts with "Error:" and nothing is booked.

## Illustration (hypothetical values)

A call with `overpayment_id` OP-1001, `payment_reference` LKP-ACH-77 and `fee_amount` 31.50 on an overpayment whose balance due was USD 400.00 returns a receipt showing a new fee entry, `fee_amount` 31.5 and `balance_due` 431.5.
